fact: INSEED presented a restitution session on 24 March 2026 saying 37,449 pastoral and agro-pastoral households were enumerated across 13 provinces into the Registre Social Unifié, and the livestock minister instructed extension to areas not yet covered.

INSEED reports that on 6 January 2026 authorities of N'Djamena's 9th arrondissement were briefed ahead of a household enrolment operation to extend the Registre Social Unifié, with WFP joining the mission.

The coordinator of the Filets sociaux said 87,500 new households of Kanem and Bahr El Gazal were registered in the Registre social unique in 2024, a registry the World Bank financed through the Filets sociaux and whose indicators on vulnerable households are available by province.
The World Bank's June 2024 appraisal for Chad's P502142 project funds US$19.5 million to strengthen the Unified Social Registry, whose deployment and extension continue by selected provinces.

INSEED reported on 24 March 2026 that 37,449 pastoral and agro-pastoral households were enrolled into the Registre Social Unifié across the 13 provinces covered by PRAPS 2, with the report still to be finalised.

The World Bank report says 1,094,784 beneficiaries, including 283,448 refugees, were registered in Chad's Unified Social Registry by 22 December 2025, and almost all beneficiaries of the Refugees and Host Communities Support Project were targeted through it.
